stem: Marco has two sticks with lengths 7 centimeters and 11 centimeters. He wants to choose a third stick whose length is a whole number of centimeters so that the three sticks, placed end to end, form a triangle. How many different lengths are possible for the third stick?
solution: For three lengths to form a triangle, each must be less than the sum of the other two.
The third length \(t\) must satisfy \(t < 7 + 11 = 18\) and \(11 < 7 + t\), so \(t > 4\).
The whole numbers with \(4 < t < 18\) are 5 through 17, which is \(17 - 5 + 1 = 13\) lengths.
verify:
ans=len([t for t in range(1,40) if t<7+11 and 7<11+t and 11<7+t])
assert Rational(spr_answers[0])==ans==13
